title: Quant sleuth session log
content:
Quick session log / investigator notes. Purpose: capture commands tried, outputs, and hypotheses for the FP8/INT8 quality/NaN regressions observed on long-chat workloads. Notes are messy — for my future self and collaborators.

---
SUMMARY:
- Intermittent NaNs when serving certain long conversational contexts (~>3k tokens) on fp8 quantized variant. Not deterministic but high frequency on particular prompt shapes (many system messages + long user history).
- Behavior differs by backend: Triton build + cuBLASLt gives NaNs earlier than native CUDA kernels on the same card.
- INT8 path passes unit tests but shows occasional quality drop (repetition/looping) not always NaN.

TIMELINE / OBSERVATIONS:
- 2025-10-28: First customer report: conversation collapsed into repeated token and then server error with NaN logits. Customer attached small repro prompt.
- 2025-10-30: Local repro attempt failed initially (no NaNs). Added KV-cache prefetch of previous 8 blocks and triggered NaN.
- 2025-11-01: Tried turning off prefix caching -> instability reduced but not eliminated.

ENVS / SETUP (common across runs):
- GPU: 80GB A100 (driver 535.86), CUDA 12.1
- Torch: 2.2.0a0+trunk local build (with cuBLASLt ops enabled)
- Runtime: redwood-serving v1.7.2 (local dev image)
- QUANT: fp8-e4m3 symmetric per-layer, INT8 asymmetric per-tensor (calibrated on a small corpus)

COMMANDS TRIED (most useful ones):
1) baseline run (native kernels):
python serve_model.py --model-path /models/mymodel --quant fp8 --cache-policy local --batch 1 --max-tokens 4096

2) force triton kernels:
TRITON_ENABLE=1 TRITON_VERBOSE=1 python serve_model.py --model-path /models/mymodel --quant fp8 --cache-policy local --batch 1

3) disable fp8 autopromotion (attempted fallback to bf16):
export REDWOOD_QUANT_FALLBACK=0  # prevent fallback to bf16 on NaN
python run_eval.py --prompt-file repro/prompts.txt --quant fp8 --repeat 5

4) kv-cache stress pattern (repro):
# create long history by repeated append
python client_sim.py --prompt "s" --repeat 200 --session-id test-01

ERROR SNIPPETS (captured stdout/stderr):
- tensor_logit = logits.max() -> includes NaN
- cuBLASLt error: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED at cublasLtMatmul:0x7f...
- runtime: sample() returned NaN in softmax input (nan in logits)

DEBUGGING STEPS / WHAT I TRIED:
- Re-ran with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 (no change).
- Pinned TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST to target architecture (compute_80).
- Recompiled with TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 (still present).
- Added per-layer clipping before softmax in a patched runtime: reduced NaN frequency but not eliminated (suggests values blowing up upstream).
- Turned off rotary embeddings: NaNs still occur -> likely not rot.
- Compared fp8 vs bf16 on same batch/seed: bf16 stable, fp8 crashes.
- Zeroed out specific attention heads at runtime (mask): sometimes avoids NaN, points to head-localized instability.
- Re-ran with deterministic RNG (PYTHONHASHSEED=42) but nondeterminism persists.

HYPOTHESES:
1) Quantization saturates dynamic range on deep kv-cache usage leading to amplification in attention scores (large dot-products -> exp overflow -> NaN).
2) Kernel numerics differ: Triton/cublaslt fp8 matmul uses different accumulation order (reduced precision acc) causing rare overflow.
3) Calibration dataset mismatch: INT8/FP8 scales computed on short sequences; when used on long-history, effective magnitudes differ and overflow.
4) Mixed-precision promotions (some ops promoted to bf16) create mismatch in scales between layers causing drift.

SAMPLE INVESTIGATIONS TO RUN NEXT:
- Recalibrate quant scales with synthetic long-history traces (generate prompts that replicate customer history) and re-run.
- Add runtime guard: if max(abs(tensor)) > threshold, recompute quant scale or force bf16 path for that layer. Log occurrences.
- Instrument attention score distributions across layers/heads (min/max/mean/std) over time to find where blow-up starts.
- Run with swapped accumulation precision: force fp32 accumulation for matmul (if possible) to test whether accumulation precision fixes NaN.
- Try using stochastic rounding off/on (if supported) to observe effect on stability.

QUICK POC COMMANDS (for next run):
# instrument attention stats and write to /tmp/att_stats.log
REDWOOD_DEBUG_ATT_STATS=1 python serve_model.py --model-path /models/mymodel --quant fp8 --cache-policy local --batch 1

# force fp32 accumulation (env toggle in local runtime)
REDWOOD_ACCUM_ACC=fp32 python serve_model.py --model-path /models/mymodel --quant fp8

NOTES TO SELF / OBSERVATION FORMATTING:
- Capture exact step (token idx) where max(abs(logits)) spikes. Useful for correlating with kv-cache entries.
- Recreate minimal reproducible prompt — try to binary search on prefix length to find smallest length that triggers NaN.
- When NaN occurs, dump per-layer activations for the last N steps (compress before storing).

CONVERSATION / LINKS TO SLACK / TICKETS:
- Slack thread: #eng-quant (see thread starting Oct 29)
- JIRA INF-1452: "FP8 instability on long chats" (customer: AcmeAI)
- GH PR: redwood/inference#2319 — earlier attempted patch to clip logits at softmax input (rollback pending more evidence)

RANDOM NOTES / WILD IDEAS:
- Could sparsity in the kv-cache (lots of repeated tokens) produce pathological attention matrices under low-precision accumulation?
- Consider per-head dynamic switching: track head stability metric and demote unstable heads to bf16 on the fly.
- Try training-aware quantization: use distillation traces from long chats to create better scale tables.

NEXT ACTIONS (short):
- Run recalibration with long-history traces (Lina) by EOD Fri.
- Add attention stat logging and run a 12h stress test in staging (Ethan owning).
- If fp32 accumulation avoids crash, prepare a short perf vs stability doc to propose as temporary mitigation.

---
End of session notes. Keep chaotic — will structure into a playbook if/when we find reproducible root cause.
